'''Larry Ray Faulkner''' (born November 26, 1944) is an American academic and businessman. He served as the twenty-seventh president of [[University of Texas at Austin|The University of Texas at Austin]] from 1998 to 2006, and as the president of the [[Houston Endowment Inc.]] from 2006 to 2012.<ref>Marquis Who's Who on the Web</ref><ref name="exxonmobil">[http://www.exxonmobil.co.uk/Corporate/investor_governance_directors.aspx ExxonMobil Board of Directors] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130420113736/http://www.exxonmobil.co.uk/Corporate/investor_governance_directors.aspx |date=2013-04-20 }}</ref>

==Biography==
===Early life===
Originally from [[Shreveport, Louisiana]], Faulkner obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in chemistry at [[Southern Methodist University]] in 1966 and his [[Ph.D.]] in chemistry from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Rotunda|year=1966|publisher=Southern Methodist University|location=Dallas, TX|page=70}}</ref>

===Career===
He taught chemistry at the University of Texas, the [[University of Illinois]], and [[Harvard University]].<ref name="exxonmobil"/> He served as provost and vice chancellor for academic affairs at the [[University of Illinois]].<ref name="exxonmobil"/> He served as president of the University of Texas at Austin from 1998 to 2006.<ref name="exxonmobil"/> On June 30, 2005, he announced that he would step down from his post in the spring of 2006. In December 2005, [[William C. Powers]] was officially named his successor and took office in February 2006. On February 9, 2006, [[University of Texas System|The University of Texas System]] Board of Regents named Faulkner president [[emeritus]], one of the system's highest distinctions.{{ref|daily_texan}} From 2006 to 2008, he chaired the National Mathematics Advisory Panel, a panel appointed by President [[George W. Bush]] to advise the President and the [[United States Secretary of Education]] on the best use of scientifically based research to advance the teaching and learning of mathematics. The final report of this panel, Foundations for Success, was released on March 13, 2008. The impact of this report on the writing of the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics can be seen in the latter's treatment of algebra. On August 13, 2010, the University of Texas at Austin's nanoscience building was named the Larry R. Faulkner Nano Science and Technology Building by the UT System Board of Regents in recognition of former president Faulkner's leadership in bringing the university's nanotechnology program to national prominence.

He sat on the board of directors of [[Guaranty Bank (Texas)|Guaranty Bank]] from December 2007 to August 2009, and of [[Temple-Inland]] from August 2005 to February 2012.<ref name="exxonmobil"/> He serves on the board of [[ExxonMobil]].<ref name="exxonmobil"/>

==Honors and awards==
*2000 [[Edward Goodrich Acheson Award|Acheson Award]] by the [[Electrochemical Society]]
*1993 Elected Fellow of The Electrochemical Society
